title: Citric Acid Anhydrous — Certificate of Analysis + REACH Safety Data Sheet

excerpt.post_processing: none — committed as the raw qpdf page slice. Normalising it would risk rewriting the inline images this fixture exists to preserve.

golden_provenance.notes: Authored from 150-DPI renders of the committed excerpt; the extractor's output was not consulted until after the golden was written. UNREVIEWED by a human.

known_defects.summary: Whole document failed to extract: 'invalid content stream'
known_defects.root_cause: strip_pdf_comments treated a '%' byte inside inline-image pixel data as a comment start and deleted to end of line, swallowing the EI terminator; Content::decode then rejected the entire page and one page failed the whole document. Acrobat writes ruled borders as 1px-tall inline images, so 18 of this file's 987 inline images carry a '%' in the payload.
known_defects.fix: src/extractor/content_stream.rs — strip_pdf_comments copies BI…ID <binary> EI verbatim (test: test_strip_pdf_comments_preserves_inline_image_data)
known_defects.evidence: pre-fix binary exits 1 on evals/pdfs/citric-acid-coa-sds.pdf; post-fix exits 0. detect-pdf failed identically.

known_defects.summary: The 3-line centred page footer becomes a fabricated 5-column table on every page, with the rest of the words spilled as loose text
known_defects.evidence: |Hampshire,|SP6|1PA,||| + |655555|Email:|…|5 of|13| followed by '19-20 Sandleheath Industrial Estate, Fordingbridge, UK Tel: 01425 Page'
known_defects.business_impact: Invents table structure in a document whose real tables matter, and destroys footer reading order.

known_defects.summary: Text painted with a white fill (`g 1`) is extracted as content
known_defects.evidence: '(Contd. of page 1)' at (460.92, 728.0) and '45.2.13' at (0, 0.32) font-size 0.96pt are absent from a 300-DPI render but present in the output on all four pages.
known_defects.root_cause: content_stream.rs honours text rendering mode 3 but not the non-stroking fill colour.
known_defects.proposed_fix: Suppress white-filled text only when no filled rect sits behind it — white-on-dark table headers are legitimate and an unconditional rule would delete them.

title: Coconut Oil - Confectionery Grade Specification (no text layer)

golden_provenance.notes: No text golden. The document has no text layer at all, so a text reference could only ever score 0% and would read as a permanent regression rather than a correct verdict. What is worth pinning is the classification: pdf2md must keep saying 'needs OCR' (exit 2) rather than silently emitting an empty document.

notes: Not a scan. This is a crisp born-digital render — 'Microsoft: Print To PDF' of an HTML page whose text was rasterised. It reads perfectly to a human and is invisible to text extraction, which is the exact shape that makes a silent empty extraction dangerous.
